messages:
incident-bot: [P1] KV cache growth + continuous-batching regression detected in production. Cache entries jumped ~10x in last 8m. Error rate up ~4% on dedicated cluster-us-west-2. Paging oncall: @Maya S

Maya S: on it. paging rotation: I'm the oncall. quick triage please — is this correlated with any deploys or flag changes? :eyes:

Alex R: noticed a config roll earlier today at 10:12 UTC — bumped `continuous_batch_window_ms` on the gpu-pool from 50 -> 220 to try to improve throughput for long sequences. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/commit/abc123

Jon P: metrics snapshot from 10:00 -> 10:10 UTC:
```
cache_entries_total: 2.3M -> 24.1M
kv_evictions/sec: 0.3 -> 12.6
p99_infer_latency_ms: 450 -> 1200
errors_5xx/min: 2 -> 85
cpu/gpu_util: 42% -> 88%
```

Samir: that looks like cache amplification due to longer batching windows — prefix KV caches keep growing because more requests are being combined and KV pages are retained longer.

Maya S: ok, mitigation plan options: 1) revert config globally, 2) toggle per-tenant batching to disable continuous batching, 3) throttles/eviction boost. Reverting globally is riskier for ongoing jobs. proposing per-customer overrides starting with heavy tenants. thoughts?

Lia K: per-tenant toggle seems safest short-term — avoids global rollback. but expect latency regressions for those customers. need to pick low-risk canary tenants.

Priya N: I have a list of top throughput tenants. small customers affected but also a few mid-market customers (orbital-ops, greatgreen) are in the mix. If we toggle for those tenants we'll need CS notifications.

Maya S: let's canary the flag off for 3 tenants: testlab, orbital-ops, smallbatch-inc. run for 10m and watch cache size + 5xxs. Command I'll run: 
```
# per-tenant feature toggle (internal tool)
rwctl feature-flag set continuous_batching false --tenant=testlab --reason="mitigate cache blowup"
rwctl feature-flag set continuous_batching false --tenant=orbital-ops --reason="mitigate cache blowup"
rwctl feature-flag set continuous_batching false --tenant=smallbatch-inc --reason="mitigate cache blowup"
```

deploy-bot: Feature flag `continuous_batching` set to `false` for tenants: testlab, orbital-ops, smallbatch-inc by Maya S. (change-id: ff-2348)

Jon P: initial canary results at +8m after toggle:
```
for tenant testlab:
  cache_entries: 1.9M -> 450k
  p99_latency: 1.1s -> 690ms
  5xx/min: 12 -> 1
for orbital-ops:
  cache_entries: 2.4M -> 600k
  5xx/min: 28 -> 2
```

Samir: good signal. continuous batching off reduced cache growth and errors. some latency increase but much lower error rate.

Maya S: start staged per-customer rollout: target next 20 high-throughput tenants over next 30m. I'll build a batch command and run in waves of 5. Lia/K please watch latency dashboards for customer-facing regressions.

Lia K: watching. setting dashboard alerts to muted for the canary tenants to avoid alert storm but will watch p95/p99 and user-facing 5xx.

Alex R: parallel task: I'll prepare a hotfix to default `continuous_batch_window_ms` back to 60 and add a safety upper-bound of 150 in config to prevent future accidental increases. planning a patch PR, will coordinate with Maya for canary deploy with config change when safe.

Priya N: I notified CS for orbital-ops and smallbatch-inc — they acknowledged and appreciate the heads-up. prepping outbound note if we scale the toggle wider.

Maya S: wave 2 executed (5 more tenants). commands: 
```
rwctl feature-flag set continuous_batching false --tenant=tenant-42
rwctl feature-flag set continuous_batching false --tenant=quant-analytics
rwctl feature-flag set continuous_batching false --tenant=pilotlabs
rwctl feature-flag set continuous_batching false --tenant=aurora-ai
rwctl feature-flag set continuous_batching false --tenant=bigindex
```

Jon P: after wave2 metrics (5m): overall cluster cache_entries dropping across affected shards, global 5xx rate down from 85->21, p99 cluster-wide trending down.

Maya S: ok continue waves. aim to finish per-customer disables for top 25 customers. then we'll flip a global config if Alex's patch is ready and tested.

Alex R: PR up: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/487. Includes: reduce default window, safety cap, telemetry to alert when `continuous_batch_window_ms` > 150 for any pool. Requesting canary on infra staging, then small prod subset.

Samir: +1 for telemetry — we need an automated rollback trigger if cache_entries spike 3x over baseline per-shard.

deploy-bot: PR 487 deployed to staging (job #4578).

Jon P: staging perf looks fine. I'll run a targeted canary of Alex's config change against one shard with synthetic load for 15m.

Maya S: after full 25-tenant pass (30m) cluster metrics: cache_entries total down 72% from peak, errors down 90%, GPU throttles normalized. No major customer-facing incidents reported for canary tenants. Great job.

Priya N: orbital-ops reports reduced failures and acceptable latency. CS updated status page draft.

Maya S: prepare a cautious global rollout: two options: 1) flip default config with safety cap (Alex's PR) then unfreeze feature flag for remaining tenants so they get safer defaults, or 2) continue per-customer toggles until PR fully validated. I'd like to do option 1 with a slow canary. any objections?

Lia K: option 1 is fine if we have automated rollbacks and telemetry. keep per-customer overrides available for outliers.

Alex R: I'll kick off canary deploy of PR 487 to 3 production shards now, monitor for 30m. If safe, we do rolling deploy.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment of PR 487 started on shards: s-05,s-12,s-21 (canary-id: c-2348).

Jon P: canary 20m in: no cache amplification on those shards, p99 slightly improved. promoting to rollout across infra.

deploy-bot: Rollout of PR 487 in progress. 12/40 shards updated.

Maya S: scaling back per-customer toggles: I'll leave overrides for top 5 tenants in case they need special handling, others will be released to new default in next 20m.

Samir: monitoring all KV eviction metrics and adding a temporary threshold alert for any shard where cache_entries increase >30% over previous 10m.

Jon P: final status update: cluster stabilizing, cache_entries trending to pre-incident baseline, 5xx rates back to nominal. Recommend closing page after 1h of stable metrics.

Maya S: agreed. creating incident ticket and postmortem: redwood-incident-2348. action items: (1) keep PR 487 in canary watch for 24h, (2) add automated rollback for window >150, (3) run runbook update for per-tenant toggle procedure, (4) CS outbound notes ready.

Priya N: ticket updated and customer comms scheduled.

Maya S: handing off to oncall-runbook for follow-up. If anything spikes re-open page. nice mitigation teamwork. :clap:

incident-bot: Page closed by Maya S. Duration: 1h12m. Incident severity: P1 -> mitigated.
